## Overview

The Gun people, also rendered Ogu, Ogun or Egun, are an ethnic group principally found in Ouémé Department in the southeast of the Republic of Benin, as well as in Lagos and Ogun State regions of southwestern Nigeria. They are Gbe-speaking people originating from the area of the old Dahomey, presently known as the Republic of Benin, and are an offshoot of the Fon people who migrated from the Kingdom of Allada. Some migrated to Badagry as early as the 15th century. The Gun account for about 15% of the indigenous population of Lagos State and 6% of the total population of the Republic of Benin. Their environment is surrounded by water, and fishing, coconut processing, salt production, trading and farming are important occupations.

## Festivals & rituals

The sources state that the Gun strongly believe in their traditions despite the fact that most of them follow other religions. They are described as worshipping a night watcher spirit called *Zangbeto*, also glossed in the source as “A Nightman.”

## Foodways

The sources describe fishing, coconut processing and salt production as activities associated with the Gun people’s water-surrounded environment. They also state that some Gun people are involved in trading and farming.

## Language & religion

Gun, also written *gungbe* in the language source, belongs to the Gbe languages group. It is spoken by the Ogu people in Benin and southwestern Nigeria, and forms part of the Fon dialectal cluster within the Eastern Gbe languages. It is close to other Fon dialects, especially the Agbome and Kpase varieties, and also to the Mahi and Weme, or Ouémé, languages. Gun is the second most spoken language in Benin and is mainly spoken in the south, including Porto-Novo, Sèmè-Kpodji, Bonou, Adjarra, Avrankou, Dangbo, Akpro-Missérété and Cotonou. It is used in some schools in the Ouémé Department. The language has three Latin-alphabet orthographies: one used in Nigeria, one developed in Benin for a Bible translation in 1923 and updated in 1975, and proposals for unification, including one made by Hounkpati Capo in 1990. The Gun people are followers of other religions as well as worshippers of *Zangbeto*.
